text:
sienna (SE): Heads-up — SiennaCorp hitting steady 429s and 2-3s tail latencies on their dedicated pool this morning. Customer says baseline is ~120 qps but they had a marketing blast up to ~420 qps for ~7m. They claim autoscale didn't keep up and a few hosts spiked CPU/GPU util.
alex (Support): Oof. Any pool name or ID? Do we have recent deployment/scale events? :eyes:
sienna (SE): Pool ID dc-9842, 4-gpu reserved (A100x4). Autoscale policy: min 4, max 8, scale step 1, cooldown 120s. They say we only reached 5 nodes despite sustained 420 qps. Baseline perf doc says A100x1 handles ~80 qps for their model/seq len.
toni (Infra): Quick math: 4 * 80 = 320 qps ideal baseline. 420 qps > 320 -> expected headroom short. If autoscale to 6 nodes they'd be at ~480 qps capacity. We need to check why we didn't hit 6.
nina (Oncall): Pulling autoscale logs + queue length for dc-9842 now. Also check auth rate-limiter and per-tenant inflight limit. Could be per-API-key throttle kicking in.
ops-bot: autoscaler-service: scale_event for dc-9842: request at 2165432250 -> evaluated_scale_to=6 -> action_queued. Actual scale_started at 2165432302 -> completed 2165432340.
alex (Support): So there was ~50s scheduling lag + infra provisioning ~38s. That explains partial undershoot during the 7m spike. Any noisy tenant signals?
toni (Infra): GPU telemetry: node-2 saw kernel saturation (nvprof high SM utilization) and host-level cgroup throttling on oom-guarded container. Active streams peaked on node-2 at 180 concurrent requests -> long queues. Looks like a hot shard (noisy neighbor) pinned to node-2.
sienna (SE): Customer says about 25% of their requests used a heavy embedding endpoint via batch call; that could cause longer per-request compute and occupy one node.
alex (Support): Repro steps requested from customer. Ask them to run a short synthetic load against the same route with headers and provide exact timestamps + sample request bodies. Suggest curl example.
sienna (SE): Sent sample curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-1","input":"<their-prompt>","max_tokens":256}'
```
They also sent server-side request pattern: 70% regular small generates (avg 60 tokens), 30% batched embedding/long-gen. Peak hour histogram attached.
toni (Infra): Actionable items:
- Increase min reserved to 6 for dc-9842 temporarily to cover expected peak. (capacity bump)
- Change autoscale cooldown from 120s -> 60s and scale_step 2 to accelerate scaling. (policy tweak)
- Add shard-balancing to move heavy batch flows off single node. (routing)
- Recommend customer enable client-side per-shard warmup and smaller batch sizes for embedding.
alex (Support): Also enable prefix KV caching for their chat route to shave tokens and reduce compute per call.
nina (Oncall): I'll open a ticket to move noisy tenant flows. Steps I'm running now:
1) mark node-2 as draining
2) reroute new streams
3) repro load on isolated node for confirmation
4) monitor queue length and 429 rate

(Will post timestamps)
ops-bot: infra: node dc-9842-node-2 set to DRAIN at 2165432380 by nina
sienna (SE): Customer ok with temporary min=6 and cooldown tweak. They asked if this will increase billing — yes? Need clear cost vs SLA note.
alex (Support): Yes — reserved capacity increase will raise committed usage. I'll send cost delta + ETA (expected 24h for full billing cycle; will confirm). Also provided short-term mitigation: enable fallback model rwd-medium-1 for non-critical requests to reduce load.
toni (Infra): Quick config snippet I'm applying:
```
{"pool_id":"dc-9842","min_replicas":6,"autoscale":{"max":8,"step":2,"cooldown_s":60}}
```
Applying now.
ops-bot: config-service: updated pool dc-9842 autoscale policy at 2165432405
nina (Oncall): Early signal: queue length fell from 480 -> 60 across pool in 90s. 429 rate dropped from 12% -> 1.6%. Latency p95 dropped 2.8s -> 620ms. Will keep monitoring for 30m.
alex (Support): Great. Next steps assigned:
- nina: full postmortem with timeline and autoscale tuning proposal (ETA 24h)
- toni: implement shard-balancer rule and investigate kernel hot-paths (ETA 48h)
- sienna: coordinate customer warmup + optional fallback rollout
- alex: cost delta + billing note to customer

sienna (SE): Thanks team. Customer asked for a small repro bundle — I saved a 60s snippet and will upload to ticket.
toni (Infra): Note for postmortem: consider autoscale pre-warm for scheduled marketing blasts and enforce per-host concurrent request soft-limit to avoid single-node hotsharding.
alex (Support): Closing loop here once postmortem + billing note shared. :thumbsup:
